notes.title: High Rez
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/2538297/521d5b732507f2f90c1ff3a9491e553068d00ab2.png[/img]

Nine years later, Inside a Star-filled Sky still stands the test of time.

It wasn't, however, working all that well on modern, high-resolution displays.  Back in the day, every monitor supported 640x480 and other 4:3 aspect ratios.

Once the resolution support was fixed, the mouse-speed mapping needed to be fixed along with it.  People with big monitors actually have faster mice.

I'm pretty sure I've setup a good, automatic method for setting your mouse speed, but there's a chance it will be too fast or slow in some situations.  It's an old game with no Settings screen, but it's not to hard to access the settings folder (browse local files on Steam) and adjust mouseSpeed.ini to your liking.

It's also time for a long overdue price-drop.

But even in its original form, people have still been playing this ancient gem.  Just a few weeks ago, someone placed a record-setting flag way up on level 8947.

I've never been that high myself, but it's insanely hard up there....

notes.title: New Release: Inside a Star-Filled Sky
notes.content:
Inside a Star-Filled Sky is now available.

Inside a Star-filled Sky is an infinite, recursive, tactical shooter by award-winning designer Jason Rohrer (Passage, Between). What if you could enter an object in a level and find a level inside of it? What if you could enter an object in that level and find another level inside of that?

What if you could change an enemy or a power-up from the inside? What if you could enter and change yourself? What if these levels inside levels inside levels went all the way down---and all the way up?

Inside a Star-filled Sky is a hard, procedurally-generated shmup built around this core concept.
